summary: August Wilhelm von Schlegel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and later under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He held professorships at Jena, Breslau, and Bonn.

Auguste Barth was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his licence at the University of Strasbourg. He taught at the Collège de Saverne and was a member of the Institut de France and the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Auguste Comte was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as Director of the Calcutta Madrasa from around 1881 to 1899 and as Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Aung San Suu Kyi, active in Tibetology and other fields, studied at the University of Delhi's Lady Shri Ram College, St Hugh's College, and SOAS University of London. She worked at the United Nations from around 1969 to 1971.

Axel Klein is a Japanologist who studied at the University of Bonn. He worked at the University of Bonn, the German Institute for Japanese Studies, and became Professor of Modern East Asian Social Studies at the University of Duisburg-Essen in 2012.

Axel Michaels is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University. He directed the Nepal Research Centre and held professorships at the University of Bern and the University of Heidelberg.

Ayu Khandro was a practitioner and scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Nyala Pema Dündul, Chokgyur Lingpa, and Drodul Pawo Dorje.

Ayya Khema was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, and Matara Sri Ñāṇarāma. She founded Wat Buddha Dhamma and served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus.

B. Alan Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and earned a Ph.D. at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, later teaching at UCSB and heading the Santa Barbara Institute for Consciousness Studies.

B. N. Goswamy was a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University from around 1950 to 1961. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from 1956 to 1958 and held a post at Panjab University from 1965 to 1998.

B. N. K. Sharma was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Madras and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. He held posts at Annamalai University, served as principal of several colleges, and taught at Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of Mumbai, Columbia University, and the University of London, and served as professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

B. R. Gopal was an Indologist and archaeologist who held posts as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India, Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India, and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica.

Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who completed a Ph.D. in World History at Moscow State University. He serves as an Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who pursued advanced study at Banaras Hindu University in 1921. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University from around 1964 to 1968.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served as Government Epigraphist for India, held leadership roles at the Archaeological Survey of India, and taught at Panjab University.

Baiei Henmi was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University from around 1915 to 1918 and held a post at Tama Art University from around 1953 to 1968.

Baihui Wu was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University, Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit, the Institute of Philosophy, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Baij Nath Puri was an Indologist and historian who earned his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow from around 1971 to 1976.
